intended_object: The Hecke operator T_p = U_p on M_k(Γ₁(N)) for p ∣ N, given by f ↦ Σ_{b=0}^{p-1} f|_k [[1, b], [0, p]], as a ℂ-linear endomorphism. This is read off the docstring and the module docs (Diamond–Shurman §5.2–5.3, Shimura §3.5).
explanation:
The underlying function is `heckeSlashUpperTri k p f = ∑ b : Fin p, f ∣[k] upperTriRep p b`, and `coe_upperTriRep` shows that `upperTriRep p b` is the matrix !![1, b; 0, p].

Mathlib's slash action carries the factor det^(k-1), as in Diamond–Shurman. So each term is p^(k-1)·p^(-k)·f((τ+b)/p), and the sum is (1/p) Σ_b f((τ+b)/p). On q-expansions this is Σ a_{np} qⁿ, the classical T_p for p ∣ N, normalized as in Diamond–Shurman.

When p ∣ N, the double coset Γ₁(N) diag(1,p) Γ₁(N) is exactly the union of the cosets of these p upper-triangular matrices. That is why the hypothesis p ∣ N is needed, and the library proves invariance under it. Since N ≠ 0, p ∣ N forces p ≠ 0, so the degenerate case is excluded. The module docs say plainly that the p ∤ N case, which needs an extra coset representative, is not built here; that is a stated scope, not an error.

The bundled map is the ℂ-linear operator on `ModularForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k`. Its linearity comes from the linearity of the slash action.

Γ₁(N) is the standard level for this operator. Mathlib has no Hecke operators on modular forms, so this does not duplicate an existing general construction.
